orig30_v2_predictions.rationale: The maintainer considers encryption out of scope for itsdangerous; users who need it should subclass the Signer to implement their own behavior.
orig30_v2_predictions.statement: Declined to add built-in encrypted cookie/secret transport support to itsdangerous, keeping encryption out of the library's scope.

orig30_v2_predictions.rationale: Expiration is embedded in the token itself, and changing any value in the token produces a completely different token, so in-place expiry extension is impossible. A non-expiring refresh token is suggested as an alternative to issue new primary tokens.
orig30_v2_predictions.statement: Do not support extending the expiry time of an already-issued token; issue a new token instead, optionally using a long-lived refresh token to issue new primary tokens.
Proposes dropping support for Python 2.6 in itsdangerous (revisiting the earlier proposal in PR #72).

orig30_v2_predictions.rationale: Support should not be removed as a spontaneous reaction; the deprecation should be reasonably long and announced in advance.
orig30_v2_predictions.statement: Proposes a reasonably long, previously announced deprecation phase for Python 2.6 support, such as a warning during installation on Python 2.6, rather than removing support immediately.
